title: Best AI Support Tools for WhatsApp Business
intro: WhatsApp carries a large share of real-time support conversations already, especially outside the US, and unlike a website widget it comes with Meta's own conversation-based messaging fees layered on top of whatever your support vendor charges — a cost dimension none of the web-chat-first tools in this category have to account for. The real question for a WhatsApp-heavy support operation isn't just whether a tool supports WhatsApp, but whether WhatsApp is treated as a first-class channel with its own automation and context, or a bolted-on integration alongside a web widget. Two of the three tools below — Crisp and Heyy — are ones this site's author has a closer relationship with (prior contributed work for Crisp, current growth and marketing employment at Heyy), so weigh those two entries as informed but not neutral, scored on the same rubric used throughout this site. These three build WhatsApp in directly rather than treating it as an afterthought.

entries.blurb: WhatsApp is one of ManyChat's three core channels, alongside Instagram and Facebook Messenger, and the same visual flow builder drives automation across all three — a comment-to-DM trigger, a keyword automation, or a broadcast campaign works the same way whether the conversation lands in WhatsApp or Instagram. AI is included starting at the $39/mo Pro tier (2,500 contacts), though it's positioned more as an add-on to flow automation than a standout conversational AI in its own right, a 3/5 in our AI Quality scorecard. The pricing model is the thing to watch most closely for a WhatsApp-heavy operation specifically: the March 2026 overhaul moved ManyChat to per-active-contact billing, and Meta's own WhatsApp messaging fees apply on top of whatever ManyChat tier you're on, so total cost has two separate usage-based components rather than one flat number. The free tier's drop from 1,000 contacts to just 25 makes it a trial rather than a viable starting point for a real WhatsApp support operation, and overage fees ($0.10/contact on Essential, down to $0.025/contact on Business) can compound quickly as your WhatsApp contact list grows — Reddit threads describe bills growing 2-3x as lists scale. Best fit if WhatsApp is one of several social-messaging channels feeding a marketing-led automation flow; a riskier bet if WhatsApp is your primary, high-volume support channel given the contact-based cost exposure.

Crisp unifies WhatsApp with web chat, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, SMS, and email in one shared inbox — the real advantage here is for a team fielding WhatsApp alongside other channels rather than exclusively, since agents work every conversation from a single thread view instead of switching between separate tools. AI automation on WhatsApp draws from the same workspace-level credit pool as every other channel — $25 of credits, roughly 450 automated conversations, at the $95/mo Essentials tier where the omnichannel inbox and workflow automation actually live. Pricing is per-workspace rather than per-contact, which sidesteps the kind of contact-count exposure that's currently the biggest complaint about ManyChat's WhatsApp offering, though Meta's own messaging fees still apply separately on top of Crisp's plan pricing, as with any WhatsApp Business API integration. Worth flagging specifically for a WhatsApp support use case: a non-trivial number of independent reviews report message-delivery reliability issues, including one Capterra reviewer describing support replies not reaching customers reliably — a real risk to weigh for a channel where message delivery is the whole point. In the interest of full disclosure, this site's author has previously written contributed content for Crisp. Good fit for a team that wants WhatsApp inside a real shared inbox alongside other channels rather than as a standalone integration; test message-delivery reliability directly before fully committing a high-volume WhatsApp queue to it.

An AI Employee deployed into a Heyy WhatsApp automation can do more than reply to messages — with the right attribute permissions enabled (Read, then optionally Update), it can capture and write contact data mid-conversation, useful for turning an anonymous WhatsApp inquiry into an identified contact record with name, email, and order history attached. Custom API actions let the same employee look up live data — order status, account state — mid-WhatsApp-thread rather than answering from a static knowledge base, which matters on a channel where customers often expect a fast, specific answer rather than a generic FAQ reply. Exit points let a team define WhatsApp-specific escalation logic in plain language — an escalate-to-human path, a refund-request path, or a custom resolution state — each explicitly wired into the automation and routed to a human inbox with full conversation history preserved when a handoff happens. WhatsApp is one of five supported channels (alongside Web Chat, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, and SMS), with no phone/voice channel documented, so this is a text-first design rather than a full contact-center replacement. In the interest of full disclosure, this site's author currently works in growth and marketing at Heyy — and the fair caveat is that pricing isn't publicly documented and there's no independent review base yet to verify these capabilities against real-world usage at scale, unlike ManyChat or Crisp's established review histories. Worth serious evaluation if WhatsApp is your primary support channel and you want an AI agent that can actively manage contact data rather than just reply, with the understanding that you're evaluating a newer, less-proven platform to get it.
